title: Why we govern them
sub: Film 8 of 10 of What an agent is: why every agent needs an owner, an identity, limits and review. Japan's first high-speed line in 1964 built its limits into the line because its trains were fast, not because they were bad. Jun's agent is capable, convincing and can't answer for what it does, so the team gives it an owner, a name of its own, limits it can't raise, and a person who checks its work.
howto: The film is drawn in the module's marble and oak. Its colours mean the same in every film: blue is tools and structure (the line along the rails, the speed allowed, the role and its locks), violet the model thinking (the agent's own log lines and its note), orange data coming back (evidence), green a check that passes or a yes, and amber a check that fails. The only red is the signal lamp of 1962.
say: eye-so, eye-ee-see, forty-two thousand and one
